and_there_is_no_clock_domain_crossing_to: the record's 'why they are different' argument needs the MAC datapath and the HC blocks to be in different clock domains. NO ABI 3.0 MODULE TAKES TWO CLOCKS, and the repository's CDC primitives -- ot_cdc_mailbox, ot_async_fifo, ot_sync_level, ot_sync_bits -- are instantiated only by rtl/ot_stage_top.sv, never by anything under rtl/abi3. As the RTL stands one clock feeds everything, so a chip holding both runs at the slower of the two.
answer: IT IS NOT. ot_compute_unit is a three-module prototype -- ot_mac_tile plus two fakeram macros -- under rtl/proto. The ABI 3.0 datapath that executes a token is ot_a3_engine_array, fourteen modules under rtl/abi3, and it does NOT instantiate ot_compute_unit or ot_mac_tile: it has its own lanes. The two designs share no module at all. So the 2.077x peak and 1.952x sustained are measured on a MAC tile prototype, and they are real for that tile; they are not a measurement of the datapath the nine-cell token matrix runs on.
not_a_claim: ot_compute_unit's 1.2897 GHz is not disputed: it is a routed, closed record with zero slew violations at a 0.8 ns target
this does not say the engine array cannot reach that clock; it says nothing has measured the engine array at all
